findings.kind: historical admission finding reconnected by current source
findings.trace: Constructor checks inward components finite and computed length > 0, then divides by that length. Vec3 length squares and sums f32 components before sqrt. For a finite component near f32::MAX, the square can overflow to +infinity under ordinary IEEE arithmetic, making the length check pass and normalization yield a zero vector. Separately, clearance is public and can later be assigned negative or nonfinite values despite the constructor gate. No normalization, ray or product was executed.
findings.conditions: A huge finite direction or subsequent invalid public clearance assignment must reach this API; ordinary producers, numerical range policy and native effects remain unestablished.

findings.direction: Determine supported directional magnitude and clearance policy, validate completed normalization and all updates as one coherent admitted outer-layer state; preserve zero clearance and inward orientation.
findings.dedup: Same historical F090, no added count.

findings.kind: historical BVH topology boundary, reconnected through current outer-layer constructor
findings.trace: OuterLayer::new forwards supplied positions and faces directly to TriangleBvh::new. TriangleBvh constructs triangle bounds by indexing every provided vertex index. An empty positions vector with a triangle containing index 0 passes the outer direction/clearance checks if those are valid and reaches an out-of-range indexed access before BVH construction. This is a source-only symbolic case, not a run or actual caller.
findings.conditions: Caller supplies a mesh whose face indices do not belong to its positions; actual producers and desired empty/degenerate policy remain open.
historical_links: 774 F054, ADDITIONAL-121 and CONTRACT-712 retain separate topology/cache and caller obligations
findings.direction: Own mesh topology and member index admission before indexed construction, preserving any intentionally supported empty triangle set.
findings.dedup: Reconnection to F054, no new count.

findings.kind: related retained-shell topology and direct outer-layer face membership boundaries
findings.trace: Shell::new invokes ShellMesh::validate, which verifies triangle indices against the initial position count. Shell.triangles is public, and later host-contact projection passes it directly to OuterLayer. OuterLayer::project validates position/velocity/mass cardinality but its child project_surface indexes each supplied face into positions without a local membership check; surface_residual does the same. A caller can independently supply an out-of-range face to these public operations, or replace Shell.triangles after initial validation and run the host-contact path.
findings.conditions: Invalid face supplied directly or via post-construction mutation, plus a reachable host-contact projection or residual; no panic, product execution or malformed ordinary producer was observed. The direct method and Shell retained topology are distinct first sites; F054 is a separate upstream outer-surface BVH constructor.

findings.kind: conditional current source observation, documented precondition and alias open
findings.trace: OuterLayer documents that all plate triangles must face inward but its constructor does not check winding. Ray/triangle intersection tests abs(determinant), admitting either facing, and BVH retains only the nearest hit. correction checks its selected triangle normal alignment afterward and returns None if alignment <= 1e-5. Thus, if a closer hit has opposing orientation and a farther aligned face also intersects within the search, the point correction does not continue to that farther face. A one-point residual can accordingly report no point correction. The child triangle-surface projection is separate and may still find or correct an overlap.
findings.conditions: The caller supplied a mesh violating the documented all-faces-inward precondition and a suitably placed nearer hit; no mesh, ray, BVH or projection executed. Input producers, actual reachability and whether to reject malformed winding or search differently are unestablished.
historical_links: Original segovb READ-L11-434 recorded ray-first/alignment policy and left actual direction/plate producer and query proof open

findings.direction: Make the documented winding precondition enforceable or define the admissible nearest-facing query behavior, while preserving one-sided, finite open plate and overlap semantics.

findings.kind: related previously identified particle aggregate, connected current outer-layer use
findings.trace: project_particles reads device positions and velocities but supplies host cached inverse_masses to project, then directly uploads positions and velocities on change. Public particle buffers may be independently replaced or written while count and cached masses stay private. If such an external native mass change succeeds, the projection can use and reupload cached rather than device mass words; readback length discrepancies can also encounter equal-length assertions.
findings.conditions: Requires independent public buffer mutation/replacement and any relevant successful native read/write, whose actual use and device behavior are unknown.
historical_links: 774 F082 and separately published /root/mhr_character xpbd-particles report retain original aggregate finding and attribution
findings.direction: Reconcile native particle buffers, count and host-mass provenance at the aggregate boundary.
findings.dedup: Related consequence of F082, not a new count.

nonfindings.text: The three particle-array lengths are asserted equal before the per-point loop, and zero mass intentionally skips prescribed particles. This does not prove face indices, numeric finiteness, or cache/device identity.

Outer projection changes current positions and velocities without resetting previous positions; subsequent SurfaceContacts uses an interval start or previous buffer for swept contact, and Shell alternates outer/surface contacts. The source provides a plausible intentional reason, not proof that phase scheduling is complete or wrong.

Buffer::write forwards to native queue and returns Ok in its body. Sequential writes do not alone prove a later ordinary wrapper Err after an earlier success; native validation, device errors and panic semantics remain open.

Body tests at 117-196 were personally displayed as text at both revisions but never executed. They state expectations, not product-validation results; the original 059/774 reviews excluded these lines.

The supplemental surface_contact.rs 370-445 window was prospectively registered but turned out to be test-source text; it was read and is preserved separately, never executed. The production 89-155 window has its own later registration.
